payload.title: 15 Best Santorini Wedding Venues With Caldera Views
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning an intimate to mid-sized guest list who will fly in from Australia via a European hub or Athens. They have chosen Santorini (or are weighing it against Mykonos and Paros) because of the caldera, and now need to decide which part of the caldera rim suits them (Oia, Imerovigli and Firostefani, Fira, the inland villages or the south caldera) and shortlist venues compared on the same terms: the caldera view, ceremony options, capacity, rooms and exclusive use.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can check availability, ceremony options and house rules for the couple's shortlisted Santorini venues on their dates and guest count.
payload.angle: Every venue in this guide passes two tests on its own official site: it hosts weddings, and it states a caldera view in words. Santorini lists usually mix cliff-top suites, wineries and beach venues with no sense of where each sits on the caldera or what the couple actually sees from the ceremony spot. This guide groups 15 venues by area along the caldera, from Oia in the north through Imerovigli and Firostefani, Fira and the inland villages to Akrotiri in the south, and gives each the same fields in the same order: the setting, the caldera view as the venue states it, ceremony options, published capacity, rooms and exclusive use (else 'Not published'), and one standout. No ranking: the order follows the caldera, so a couple can choose an area first and a venue second.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: Santorini's caldera wedding areas (Oia; Imerovigli and Firostefani; Fira; Pyrgos, Megalochori and the inland villages; Akrotiri and the south caldera) and that the right one depends on guest count, ceremony type and the view the couple wants; link /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding prominently for the planning steps and the hub /destinations/europe/greece.
At a glance: mobile-friendly comparison table with 5 columns (venue, area, caldera view setting, ceremony options, capacity) with 'Not published' where a field is not published.

How to compare like for like: venue type (cliff-top hotel, private venue with exclusive use, winery), ceremony on site, seated capacity, rooms on site, exclusive use. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (house rules not published are confirmed in writing by the Wedded Advisor), plus a link to /wonderland-concierge.
Choosing an area: practical guidance per area as official tourism or venue sources state it; no unsourced distances, drive times or sunset claims.

Two-part inclusion rule applied to every entry: a live read of the venue's own official site says it hosts weddings AND states a caldera view in words. Never snippets alone, never photos. Target 15; if fewer qualify the title count changes and the person is told; no padding. Non-luxury qualifiers held back as reserves.

15 venues grouped by area (Oia; Imerovigli and Firostefani; Fira; Pyrgos, Megalochori and the inland villages; Akrotiri and the south caldera), each with the same fields in the same order: area and setting; the caldera view as the venue states it (fresh wording, not quoted research talk); ceremony options as stated; capacity, rooms and exclusive use where published, else 'Not published'; one standout. No ranking; order follows the caldera north to south.
Getting there: Santorini airport, Visit Greece flight time, Smartraveller ferry advice (from content/posts/santorini-wedding/03-source-pack.json); no port claims; no transfer arrangements.
When to marry: HNMS Naxos averages labelled as the nearest official station; Smartraveller heat, wildfire, earthquakes and volcanic activity; no 'best month'.

Legal in brief: Smartraveller and Embassy Athens facts as at November 2026, dated once; 'check with the Municipality of Thira and the embassy, including any fees'; link /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding for the full steps; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once. Nothing on church or religious paperwork.

FAQ (4 to 6): Which part of Santorini is best for a caldera wedding? Can we book a Santorini venue for exclusive use? How many guests can a Santorini venue hold? How do guests get to Santorini? Can Australians legally marry in Santorini?

Close: shortlist with a Wedded Advisor (brand-facts claims only). Links: /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destination-weddings/mykonos-wedding-venues, /destination-weddings/paros-wedding-venues, /wonderland-concierge (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge'), /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-venues&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing.
avoid: Any price, fee, minimum spend or amount; any capacity, room count, distance or time not on an official source.
'Best' ranking claims in copy (the title keeps '15 Best' as given, the body does not rank); numbering that implies rank; 'best month'.
Caldera views inferred from photos or snippets; venues without a weddings offer on their own site; beach venues without a stated caldera view; venues off Santorini.

Research talk in copy ('on its own site', 'in its own words', 'does not publish' as our search, page dates as source talk, what we could or could not confirm, myths); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once; linking a source more than once.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, booking or review sites, Facebook groups, Instagram, Pinterest or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.
Linking /venue/rocabella-santorini-hotel-spa (its domain is for sale) or the old page /7-must-see-santorini-destination-wedding-venues.
Vendor names other than venues; venue contact or business details; transfer arrangements; port claims; implying partnerships or preferred rates.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; 'from first idea to the last dance' and 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text; legal, church or religious paperwork detail.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day, breathtaking), exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; images other than placeholders until licensed or press kit with permission.
